variant-first.note: Set A contains numerous misbindings of dimensions to the wrong elevation: 9' - 2", 4 1/2", 9' - 11 1/2", 8' - 8", 3' - 6" and 9' - 10 1/4" are attached to South/West/North Bedroom elevations where those values do not appear (e.g. 8' - 8" and 3' - 6" belong to A1 South Bedroom, 9' - 2" and 4 1/2" to C5 North Bedroom), and it invents an 'Artwork … center point X' measurement and an 'above MWD01' condition. Set A does correctly capture the C1 North Living dimensions, the artwork note, TV/MWL01 in C3 West Living and the A1 scale-related facts, but its repeated use of the label 'SOUTH BEDROOM ELEVATION A3 WEST' (A3 is the West Bedroom) corrupts several claims. Set B is mostly value-faithful and gets the A1 scale, MWL01/TV in West Living and the C3 segment dimensions right, but many claims are vague ('interior elevation', 'Wall section', 'room elevation') and it also misassigns 7' - 6" to North Bedroom and 9' - 10" to South Bedroom. Overall B makes far fewer outright misread or invented claims, so it is the better set despite its vagueness.

baseline-first.note: Set A misbinds several values to the wrong detail: it assigns W8X13 to B1 FLOOR BEAM NEAR GRID 5 and W10X15 to E6 (both are reversed — B1 is W10X15, C1/E6 are W8X13), puts 10'-0" and 8" on details (near Grid 5, E6) whose dimension strings contain no such values, and gives FLOOR BEAM @ GRID 4 a 5'-0" length that actually belongs to the B4/FLOOR BEAM @ GRID 3 detail. Set B correctly ties W10X15 to A4, B1 and Grid 5 beams, ø 3" to the C1 and E6 roof beams, and 4'-2"/3'-1" to the B1 (FLOOR BEAM NEAR GRID 5) detail. Set B's main errors are calling the 2" dimension a 'top flange width' on Detail B4 and assigning 2'-6" to Detail C4, where that dimension does not appear (it belongs to C1). Both sets contain vague, unlocalized opening claims, but Set B keeps conditions and values consistently bound to the correct details.

Both sets capture the core elevations (finished floor 2'-9 1/2" and grade 0'-0") and room containment, and both repeat the same misread value 2'-3 1/2" for the Living Room finished floor, which is not on the page. Set A adds several misbound or trivial claims: grid marker K treated as the Centre Module's location, sheet number A302 as a room 'location', 'WEST MODULE | location | West' as tautology, and detail bubble A1 treated as a drawing number for the scale. Set B instead correctly binds the 3/8"=1'-0" scales to the Living Room Section (A1) and Centre Module section (C1), and adds supported sheet metadata (A-302, BUILDING SECTIONS, lot number 116). Set B's only other weakness is the 'West Module adjacent to Centre Module' claim, whose quote does not itself support adjacency.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core elevations and room containment, but Set A also correctly records the sheet number A-302, sheet title BUILDING SECTIONS, lot number 116, and the A1/C1 scales, which Set B omits. Set B adds several vague or misbound claims (CENTRE MODULE 'location K' where K is a grid line, MECHANICAL ROOM 'location Building Section A302', WEST MODULE 'location West', and generic 'building section contains room' entries) plus repeated duplicate finished-floor claims. Both sets share one misread value: the Living Room finished floor is 2' - 9 1/2" in the source, not 2' - 3 1/2". Set A's only other weakness is a quote for the West/Centre adjacency that does not itself support the relation.

Set B makes more serious errors: it misreads the faucet model as SP-L-65014LF-PC and the shower head model as 2655, truncates SK's manufacturer to "FR" and description to "SI", and misbinds F1's description as "FA" when F1 is a BED. variant-first.note: Set B binds nearly all values correctly and completely (e.g., SH model 52655, FAUCET model BSP-L-65014LF-PC with its F2 tag, MWD02 and MWL01 dimensions), whereas Set A repeatedly truncates or garbles values: SK manufacturer 'FR' (FRANKE), SK description 'SI' (SINK), FAUCET model 'SP-L-65014LF-PC', SHOWER HEAD '2655', and WB profile missing 'MDF'. Set A also misreads F1's description as 'FA' when the schedule lists BED, and drops the material from the wall base profile. baseline-first.note: Set A captures the full revision history (marks 1–5 with dates and descriptions), the lot number, and the section scales, all supported by the title block and sheet text. baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the main member sizes (L3x3x1/4 angle, 3" STD pipe, 4 1/2x4 1/2x1/2 plate, 3/4" bolts and holes, 1 1/2" hole, T.O. STEEL 11'-4"), but Set B introduces several unsupported bindings: a 'PV POST base plate edge distance' of 2", a weld size with an invented 'top connection' condition, a 'typical' condition and quote for T.O. variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core C3/A5 crane-attachment callouts (3" STD pipe, 4-1/2x4-1/2x1/2 plate, (2) 3/4" bolts, 1-1/2" hole, 1" plate, 1/4" weld) and both make the same misread of the PL 3"x3/8"x1'-6" plate as an "angle." STEEL 11'-4" TYP," plus heavy duplication. baseline-first.note: Set A binds the tile, wallboard, gable and bracket facts cleanly and captures the detail scales (D1/D3/D5 at 6"=1'-0", D5 at 1 1/2"=1'-0"), the 3/8" porcelain wall tile, lot number and project name, with quotes that match the text. BATHROOM FLOOR as a finish value, plus it omits the porcelain wall tile and all detail scales and repeats several claims. variant-first.note: Set B captures the title-block and detail facts (lot number 116, BOREALIS, the 6"=1'-0" and 1 1/2"=1'-0" detail scales) and binds the gable, porcelain wall tile and glass tile data correctly. Set A invents a '3" SUBFLOOR' thickness by splicing the shower-pan dimension with the SUBFLOOR label, and misbinds 'P3' (a finish code) to the steel L-bracket attachment. A also adds unsupported conditions ('top layer', 'boundary') and several trivial/duplicate claims, while B's few weaknesses are mainly vague entities (e.g. 'surface | finish | PT1', 'edge strip | presence').

baseline-first.note: Both sets mix sound section callouts (W10X15, W8X10, C3X6, L4X4X5/16, HSS 4x4x1/4 with keynote 05) with loose dimension grabs, but Set A also captures genuinely supported items Set B misses, notably the 1 1/2" = 1'-0" detail scale and the PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 plate size. variant-first.note: Set A binds values to the correct member types and detail locations more often, correctly identifying C3X6 as a channel, W10X12/W10X15 as beams and HSS4X4X1/4 with detail conditions (C1/C2, A5), and it captures the 11 1/2" framing spacing that B omits. Set B preserves more useful context (grid locations, section references, and the grade-to-first-floor and first-floor-to-T.O.-steel vertical relationships) and avoids the vague, condition-less 'dimension/structural member' claims that fill Set A. Set A repeatedly invents or misassigns conditions — 'lower level', 'bottom level', and 'Detail A1' for dimensions (1'-8 7/16", 1'-8", 8", 10") and W10X15 that appear in other sections — and duplicates several claims. baseline-first.note: Set A captures the title-block facts (client, website, revision dates/descriptions) and the material callouts (QZ countertop, 1/2" MDF finished with P3, bulkhead clad and finished with P3) with supporting quotes. variant-first.note: Set B captures the title-block and project facts correctly (revision dates/descriptions, client, website) and binds the platform clearance condition ('MIN. 12" CLEAR ABOVE AND 1" EITHER SIDE') properly, while Set A offers none of these and repeats the 2"x6" framing claim three times. Set A also invents conditions not on the page ('excluding 6" offset', 'from left edge to counter transition'), mis-binds SK to MWK04 as a sink component, uses an entity ('Upper Millwork') that does not appear, and states 8 ft where the quoted dimension is 8' - 4". Set B is not clean either — 'SK = skirt', the dining-table 6" clearance, the BOREALIS project name and the 4' - 0" width attributed to the DIRTT Breathe wall are unsupported bindings — but its errors are fewer and its correct claims more numerous and better conditioned.

Set A binds the key fabrication facts correctly — SIP thickness with vapor barrier, 3" steel decking, 3/4" exterior-grade plywood, PL 8 x 3/8 with 7/16" holes at 12" O.C., lag screw with washer, and the sealant/waterproofing notes — with mostly supporting quotes. Overall A is more faithful and has fewer substantive errors, though both sets pad with repeated/trivial entries.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures more substantively correct claims — SIP thickness with vapor barrier, exterior-grade plywood, 3" steel decking, W10x15 beam section, plate hole diameter/spacing, and bolt size and head type — while Set A duplicates the same joist/frame/grade-level claims several times and adds garbled or misbound ones (e.g. 'ank nail', 'deck thickness 3/4"' bound to FIRST FLR, and W10 X 15 merged with 3" steel decking as one specification). Both sets misbind the 5'-2 1/2" and 8'-0" dimensions (they belong to the A1 deck module detail, not railing post spacing or deck connection spacing), and B also mislabels the 8'-0" as an A3 connection length. A additionally invents unsupported relations (scaffold footing 'connection: frame', bracket 'connection to joist') and offers tautological claims, so B is the cleaner and more faithful set overall.

Set A captures the full revision table (dates and descriptions for revisions 1–5), the scale of both sections, and the lot number, whereas Set B omits all revision history and scale information. variant-first.note: Set B captures the revision table (marks 1–5 with dates and descriptions) and the two section scales (3/8" = 1'-0" for C1/West Module and A1/East Module), all supported by the text layer, whereas Set A omits these entirely and instead repeats the same grade/finished-floor elevations four times. Both sets correctly state finished floor 2' - 9 1/2" above grade 0' - 0" for both modules and lot number 116.

BE 1/4\"" and a weld symbol misread as slope), and both invent dimension conditions, but A's errors are fewer relative to its larger body of correct, well-bound claims.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures the key Module Link facts (W10X15, 3/4" bolts with quantity, 5"X3/8" support plates, the 2'-9 1/16" and 3'-0 13/16" dimensions) and the continuous bent plate 7.5X3X1/4", all of which Set A omits. Set B's faults are mainly duplicated claims and invented dimension qualifiers (e.g. 'from grade level to mid-plate') and one quote ("1/4\" R") not present in the text layer, but it is materially more complete and better bound.

Set A captures the sheet's substantive facts — the 40-tube solar thermal array (2 X APSE-20), the 1/4"=1'-0" drawing scale, finished floor at 2'-9 1/2" above grade, and the note that layered swing lines indicate both tilt and turn door operation — all supported by their quotes. variant-first.note: Set B captures important facts Set A misses, notably the 40-tube quantity (2 X APSE-20), the 1/4" = 1'-0" drawing scale, the tilt-and-turn door operation note, and the window/door tag bindings (1.14 W5, 1.01 D1, 1.13 W6), all supported by the text. baseline-first.note: Set A captures more of the page's real engineering facts — the 28" dia footing, 3" std pipe, 3/4" bolt, PL5X3/8 fitted stiffener, 14/16 gauge deck plates, 6" min each side of opening, and the >6" dia reinforcement threshold — with quotes that support them. variant-first.note: Set A captures four title-block facts — sheet title FRAMING ISOMETRICS, lot number 115, and drawn by / checked by TEAM CAPITOL DC — all of which are supported by the text layer and the title block shown in the image. A binds dimensions to the right bays and datums (Bay B-C = 3'-1", 7'-6" bay spacing, L4X4X5/16 on the South elevation, T.O. Steel and First Floor kept relative to Grade Level), whereas B assigns 10'-0" to the B–C bay (the middle bay is 3'-1") and corrupts several values ('7 ft-in', '5 ft-in', '10 ft', '18 ft', '32'-0" ft-in').
